B02-L01 - From notebook task to reusable script contract
What you already know as an analyst: notebook cells can load, clean and summarize data.
What changes in engineering: the run begins from one deliberate entry point and receives explicit paths/config.
Why engineers care: another run, machine or scheduler cannot depend on your forgotten cell state.
Small worked example: main(input_path, output_path) coordinates load -> transform -> validate -> publish.
Real engineering version: C3 will add project packaging, dependency environments, CLI design and tests.
An analyst notebook can succeed because cells were run in a lucky order. An engineering-style script must succeed from a clean
start with explicit inputs, outputs and failure boundaries.
Turn a familiar notebook workflow into a reusable script contract with an entry point, explicit paths and no hidden notebook state.
Course 1 PY0/PY9/PY10: you can run a notebook, save outputs and explain reproducibility. No command-line or packaging
Picture a kitchen recipe. A notebook can contain half-used bowls already on the counter. A script contract starts with an empty
kitchen: it names ingredients, steps, output and what happens if an ingredient is missing.
5. New words before we use them
script - a Python file intended to run as a program
entry point - the place execution intentionally begins
hidden state - a value/file/object that exists only because something earlier happened outside the declared run
contract - the declared inputs, outputs, rules and failure behavior
Official Modules + pathlib are authority. No video is required. If you need a visual, use the B02-L03 pathlib companion later.
Copy one simple C1 analysis flow into a fresh .py file. Restart Python, run only that file, and record the exact input path, output
A clean process creates the same output without you manually running setup cells first.
C2B DA-to-DE Bridge | B02 Python Pipeline Transition | INTERNAL QA RC1
main() makes the start explicit; paths enter the workflow instead of hiding in notebook state; validation runs before publish.
- Copying every notebook cell unchanged into one giant script.
- Using current working directory assumptions you cannot explain.
- Creating final output before validation finishes.
- Treating if __name__ == "__main__" as magic syntax instead of an entry-point boundary.
1) Locate the single input file. 2) Make a tiny load-only main(). 3) Print/record row count. 4) Add one function at a time. Do not add venv/CLI
Create a fresh script that reads sales_2026_02.csv and writes a new CSV to an outputs folder. Input/output paths must be
arguments to main(), not scattered constants.
Restart the interpreter and rerun. Compare output row count to source; prove output is new and source bytes are unchanged.
In 60-90 seconds explain notebook state vs a clean-start script and name one hidden dependency that could break automation.
Save the first attempt. Only then open Review B02-L01. Close it and rebuild the same contract using sales_2026_03.csv and a different output
Save script, command/run method, source/output paths, source/output row counts, one failure/recovery note, confidence 1-5. PASS ->

B02-L02 - Functions, modules and decomposition for
What you already know as an analyst: functions reduce repeated notebook code.
What changes in engineering: functions also create failure/test boundaries and separate I/O from transformation.
Why engineers care: you can diagnose, replace or test one stage without rewriting the run.
Small worked example: require_columns(df, required) raises before bad data reaches merge.
Real engineering version: C3 will turn these into project modules/packages with automated tests.
A pipeline becomes hard to test when loading, cleaning, validation and publishing are tangled in one block. Small explicit
functions let you isolate failure and reuse only the part that should change.
Decompose a workflow into coherent functions with explicit inputs/returns, and understand the module as a reusable file
B02-L01 mastered; C1 practical Python functions are familiar.
Imagine four labeled workstations: LOAD, TRANSFORM, VALIDATE, PUBLISH. If a result is wrong, you inspect the relevant
station instead of dismantling the whole factory.
5. New words before we use them
function contract - what a function accepts, returns, changes and may raise
module - a Python file that can define reusable code
side effect - a change outside the returned value, such as writing a file
pure-ish transform - a transformation that mostly depends on explicit inputs and returns an output without hidden external changes
Python Modules is the current authority. A separate functions video is unnecessary because C1 already taught function syntax.
Take your L01 script and split it into load_sales(), transform_sales(), validate_sales() and publish_sales(). For each, write one
main() becomes short and readable; each function has one coherent responsibility.
C2B DA-to-DE Bridge | B02 Python Pipeline Transition | INTERNAL QA RC1
Decomposition makes dependencies visible. A schema error can fail in validation without being confused with output-writing
- A function secretly reads a global dataframe instead of accepting it.
- Validation function silently edits data to make checks pass.
- Catching every exception inside each function and returning None.
Start with only two functions: load and validate. Make them work. Then isolate transformation; publish is last.
Add a reusable require_columns() function and use it against the missing-column fixture. It must fail with a useful message
Run against good monthly data and the missing-column fixture. Good input passes; bad input fails before transform/publish.
Explain why a function can make code easier to operate even when it does not reduce total lines.
After saved attempt, review L02; then change the required schema by adding source_file and prove the validator catches its absence.
Save module/script, written function contracts, good/bad run output, failure message and changed retry. PASS -> L03.

B02-L03 - Deterministic file discovery and multi-file batches
What you already know as an analyst: pd.read_csv("file.csv").
What changes in engineering: discover a declared batch, sort it, validate every member and keep source lineage.
Why engineers care: missing/extra/changed files can silently alter production results.
Real engineering version: C3-01 adds landing metadata, historical batches, incremental state and backfill rules.
Real recurring data often arrives as a folder of files. Hard-coding January, February and March is fragile: April arrives and your
Discover matching files deterministically, sort them, preserve source_file lineage, verify schemas and reconcile combined rows to
L01-L02 mastered; you can read one CSV.
Think of an airport baggage belt. Each bag has a tag showing where it came from. You do not just dump bags into one pile; you
list which bags arrived, in a predictable order, and keep the tag after combining them.
5. New words before we use them
file discovery - finding inputs by declared path/pattern rather than manual list
deterministic - same valid inputs/rules produce the same selection/order/result
lineage - evidence of where a row/file came from
batch - a bounded group of records/files processed together
Book + current pathlib documentation are primary. The previously added Real Python YouTube companion remains recorded in
the source audit, but no exact useful segment could be independently reverified, so it is not assigned as required learner media.
Discover the three monthly files, save their ordered names and each row count, add source_file, combine them, and reconcile the
assert len(sales) == sum(len(p) for p in parts)
Exactly three source filenames in sorted order, 32 rows from each, 96 combined rows, and every combined row has lineage.

The pattern is data-driven rather than calendar-code-driven; lineage survives concatenation; reconciliation proves no file was
- Glob pattern accidentally includes outputs or failure fixtures.
Print the matched paths first. Do not concatenate until the list is exactly the intended batch. Then inspect columns for each file.
Create a temporary folder containing only two copied monthly files. Point the same discovery function at it; no code changes
Expected file count and actual file list are saved; combined rows equal sum of component rows; source_file counts reproduce file
Explain why sorted discovery + lineage is more reliable than a hard-coded filename list.
Review after attempt; then add a renamed nonmatching CSV and prove it is excluded by the contract rather than accidentally ingested.
Save discovered paths, per-file rows/schema, combined rows, lineage count, changed-folder retry. PASS -> L04.

B02-L04 - pandas merge and validation contracts for
What you already know as an analyst: merge two DataFrames and inspect result.
What changes in engineering: assert master uniqueness, declare many_to_one, measure unmatched keys, reconcile rows/totals.
Why engineers care: pipeline joins need executable contracts, not visual confidence.
Small worked example: current customers.csv deliberately contains two C013 rows.
Real engineering version: C3 uses similar checks as automated data tests and referential-integrity controls.
A merge that returns rows is not proof of correctness. A duplicate lookup key can multiply business rows and still create a
Validate lookup-key uniqueness before merge, use pandas merge cardinality validation, quantify unmatched keys and reconcile
L03 mastered; C1 PY5 merge and join/cardinality concepts are familiar.
A customer master should behave like one ID card per customer. If customer C013 has two different ID cards, attaching
customer attributes to orders becomes ambiguous; do not choose one silently.
5. New words before we use them
many-to-one - many fact rows may match one master row
validate= - pandas merge parameter that checks expected key cardinality
unmatched key - fact-side key with no master match
critical quality gate - a failed rule that blocks publish
pandas.merge 3.0.5 is authority. Note its documented null-key behavior differs from SQL and is one reason explicit validation
Try the many_to_one merge with supplied customers.csv. Save the failure. Identify C013. Do not drop one row. Then create an
in-memory clean demonstration master only after documenting that the fixture is intentionally ambiguous, and prove row count
enriched = sales.merge(customers, on="customer_id", how="left", validate="many_to_one", indicator=True)
The uncorrected merge is blocked. Your evidence names C013 before publish. A separately controlled demonstration merge

The pipeline refuses an ambiguous master instead of turning a data-quality problem into duplicate business events.
- Using many_to_many because it makes the error disappear.
- Checking only final row count and not unmatched keys.
- Treating null-to-null pandas matching as SQL-equivalent behavior.
Check customers.customer_id.value_counts().head(). Then test is_unique. Stop there until you can explain why C013 is ambiguous.
Create a tiny fresh orders/master pair with a different duplicated master key. Prove your same validator blocks it without code
Master uniqueness checked before merge; merge cardinality declared; fact rows reconciled; unmatched keys counted; monetary
Explain why duplicate dimension/master keys are not safely repaired by arbitrary deduplication.
Review after saved attempt; changed retry uses a different duplicate key and one unmatched fact key.
Save duplicate-key evidence, blocked merge message, controlled demonstration, row/unmatched/total checks. PASS -> L05.

B02-L05 - CSV, JSON and Excel interfaces with explicit
What you already know as an analyst: read_csv/read_excel/read_json.
What changes in engineering: declare parsing assumptions and output grain; preserve source; validate serialized output after writing.
Why engineers care: format conversion can lose types, rows or nested meaning.
Small worked example: nested_orders has 5 orders but 10 item rows.
Real engineering version: C3-01 adds defensive parsers, Parquet, landing metadata and schema-drift handling.
A file extension does not tell you the business meaning of a row. CSV, nested JSON and Excel each need explicit parsing and
Treat CSV/JSON/Excel as interface contracts: encoding/header/schema/type assumptions, nested-record grain, immutable
L03-L04 mastered; C1 can load files and reshape data.
Imagine the same shipment arriving in three boxes. One box is flat rows (CSV), one contains boxes inside boxes (JSON), and
one is a presentation workbook (Excel). You must know what each layer means before unpacking.
5. New words before we use them
serialization - a way of representing data in a file/message format
nested record - an object containing child objects/arrays
normalization - turning nested structure into a chosen tabular grain
read-back validation - reopening the published file to prove the saved artifact matches intended data
Optional Corey pandas I/O: 0:56-3:20 CSV; 6:15-12:18 Excel; 12:18-16:59 JSON. After each, use the supplied local files.
pandas 3.0.5 IO tools | Python 3.14.7 json | Corey pandas I/O visual

10 items. Inspect monthly_report_template.xlsx without overwriting it; write output to a new filename and re-read only if your
print("declared grain: one row per order item")
Your notes distinguish 5 order objects from 10 item rows. Template remains byte-identical. Any created output is separate and

- Assuming JSON list length equals desired output rows.
- Using Excel formulas as the hidden source of business truth.
- Relying on automatic dtype inference for critical fields.
Do CSV and JSON first. For Excel, inspect the supplied README sheet; if your local Excel writer engine is unavailable, save CSV evidence
and record Excel output as environment-dependent rather than faking it.

Explain why "JSON contains 5 orders" and "normalized table contains 10 rows" can both be correct.

Save parsing contract, normalized sample, counts, template-integrity proof and changed retry. PASS -> L06.

B02-L06 - HTTP API basics for data acquisition
What you already know as an analyst: open/download a file manually.
What changes in engineering: retrieval becomes code with timeout/status/parse validation and an explicit failure path.
Why engineers care: networks fail and a 200 response can still contain unexpected data.
Small worked example: local api_response.json contains 4 region metrics.
Real engineering version: C3-01 teaches authentication, pagination, rate limits, retries/backoff and API contracts in depth.
Data does not always arrive as a file. APIs are a common interface, but a successful HTTP connection is not the same as
Understand request/response, GET, status codes, timeout, JSON response parsing and an offline fixture fallback. Authentication,
pagination, rate limits and retry strategy are intentionally deferred to C3.
L05 mastered; no previous API experience required.
An API is like a service counter. You send a request slip to an address; the counter sends a response with a status and a
package. You check the status before trusting the package.
5. New words before we use them
HTTP - a protocol for requests and responses on the web
endpoint - a specific API URL for a resource/action
GET - a request method commonly used to retrieve data
status code - numeric response outcome such as 200 or 404
timeout - maximum wait before treating a request as failed
Requests 2.34.2 Quickstart is authority. Recommended visual: Real Python, Consuming APIs - GET and POST, 01:50-03:02
only (GET -> Response -> .json() -> status code). After watching, immediately run the supplied offline fixture and then the
optional local-HTTP GET. The older Corey Requests video remains preserved as backup only. Do not study auth/pagination here
Requests 2.34.2 Quickstart | Real Python - Consuming APIs: GET and POST (01:50-03:02) | Corey Requests visual - preserved backup
First parse Practice_Data/api_response.json offline and validate four metrics. Then, if local HTTP is available, serve the
Practice_Data folder locally and GET that same file with timeout + raise_for_status().
Offline and local-HTTP paths produce the same four metric records; network failure does not create/publish a fake empty

Retrieval and validation are separate. timeout bounds waiting; status checking exposes HTTP failure; JSON parsing handles the
response body only after transport succeeds.
- Ignoring status_code and parsing error pages as data.
- Returning [] on every exception and calling the run successful.
- Trying to master pagination/auth here and duplicating C3.
Use offline fixture only; mastery does not require public internet. Explain the hypothetical request/response path, then prove parsing/validation
Write a function that accepts either local JSON path or URL mode through config. Both paths must feed the same
Status/path source recorded; exactly four region metrics; required keys present; failed retrieval cannot reach publish.
Explain the difference between "HTTP request succeeded" and "the data is valid".
After review, point the local mode at service_metrics.json or another provided JSON and adapt only the validation contract, not retrieval
Save offline validation, local HTTP evidence if available, timeout/status code logic, one failure route. PASS -> L07.

B02-L07 - Error handling, failure classification and
What you already know as an analyst: fix an error interactively and rerun a cell.
What changes in engineering: the code must expose what failed, with context, and stop or quarantine according to policy.
Why engineers care: nobody may be watching the run live.
Small worked example: sales_bad_numeric contains order 1006 with unit_price="oops".
Real engineering version: C3 adds transient retry policy, orchestration failures and incident recovery.
A pipeline that hides an error can be more dangerous than one that crashes. The goal is not "no exceptions"; it is to classify
failure, add context, contain damage and block unsafe publish.
Distinguish missing-input, schema, parse, quality and network failures; catch only what you can contextualize/recover from; raise
meaningful errors; quarantine or block deliberately.
L06 mastered; basic try/except syntax may be familiar but no engineering error strategy is assumed.
Think of circuit breakers. A small problem in one appliance should not burn the house. Some failures can be isolated; critical
ones cut power before damage spreads.
5. New words before we use them
exception - a runtime signal that normal execution cannot continue as written
classification - naming the kind of failure so the correct recovery is chosen
containment - preventing a bad condition from contaminating later output
quarantine - separating invalid records for review instead of silently mixing/dropping them
Python Errors and Exceptions is authority. Optional Corey try/except: roughly 00:21-03:00 covers missing-file and
Python 3.14.7 Errors and Exceptions | Corey try/except visual
Run the bad-numeric fixture through a strict parser and save the failure. Run missing-column fixture through require_columns().
Classify each as parse vs schema failure and prove final publish is not called.
The evidence identifies one malformed numeric at order 1006 and missing customer_id in the second fixture. Neither failure
C2B DA-to-DE Bridge | B02 Python Pipeline Transition | INTERNAL QA RC1
Specific validation turns vague downstream wrong totals into early, contextual failures; failure boundary sits before
- Coercing bad numeric to 0 without policy/evidence.
- Logging ERROR and continuing to publish anyway.
- Deleting a malformed row and calling it "cleaning" with no quarantine/control.
Test one failure at a time. First assert required columns. Then numeric parsing. Save the exact exception before writing recovery logic.
Create a copied input with one invalid discount_pct > 1.0. Classify it as business-quality failure (not parse failure) and block
Failure type, affected row/key, policy (block/quarantine), output-withheld proof and clean-input pass are all recorded.
Explain why "caught the exception" is not automatically a successful recovery.
Open review only after attempt; changed retry uses a different malformed field and requires the same containment behavior.
Save exception messages, failure classification table, output-withheld evidence, clean rerun. PASS -> L08.

B02-L08 - Logging, run evidence and validation gates
What you already know as an analyst: print(df.shape) and inspect manually.
What changes in engineering: save timestamped run events plus structured checks that can be reviewed later.
Why engineers care: unattended jobs need reconstructable evidence and objective pass/fail controls.
Small worked example: customer_key_unique FAIL must block publish even if Python raised no unexpected exception.
Real engineering version: C3-08 expands this into observability, incidents, lineage and DataOps.
When a pipeline runs without you watching, you need evidence of what happened and whether the data passed rules. Logs
describe events; validation results describe trust.
Use meaningful log levels, create machine-readable validation results, distinguish operational success from data-quality success,
and gate publish on critical checks.
A flight has two records: the black-box event log and the safety checklist. "The engines ran" does not prove "the aircraft was safe
to depart." Pipeline logs and validation results play different roles.
5. New words before we use them
log level - severity label such as INFO/WARNING/ERROR
observability evidence - recorded signals that help reconstruct what a run did
validation result - structured check with rule/status/observed value
publish gate - decision point that prevents final output when critical checks fail
Python 3.14.7 Logging HOWTO is authority. Optional Corey Logging Basics: full 14:25; focus on replacing print, log levels, file
Python 3.14.7 Logging HOWTO | Corey Logging Basics
Create run.log and validation_results.json for the practice batch. Record discovery count, raw rows, parse result, master
uniqueness and reconciliation. Make customer uniqueness a critical check.
run.log tells chronological events; validation_results.json exposes customer_key_unique=FAIL on the supplied ambiguous

The validation schema is machine-readable and independent from human prose logs. A critical FAIL has an enforced
- Passwords/tokens or private data written to logs.
- A JSON check says FAIL but code still publishes.
- Using logs instead of an independent numeric reconciliation.
Start with three events: run_started, inputs_discovered, validation_complete. Then create only two checks: expected_file_count and
Add a net_sales reconciliation check with tolerance 0.01 and prove it passes on the three good monthly files.
Saved log exists; validation JSON parses; each check has rule/status/observed; at least one controlled FAIL blocks publish.
Explain why "no ERROR log" does not prove a dataset is trustworthy.
After review, add one fresh schema check and inject its failure. Do not change logging setup to solve the data problem.
Save run.log, validation_results.json, publish-gate decision, changed-failure retry. PASS -> L09.

B02-L09 - Recurring batch execution and safe rerun
What you already know as an analyst: rerun a notebook/report manually.
What changes in engineering: define what repeat execution is allowed to change and prove duplicate business rows are not accumulated.
Why engineers care: schedulers will eventually rerun jobs after retries/failures.
Small worked example: write a complete output snapshot to a controlled path rather than append unchanged monthly rows every run.
Real engineering version: C3 teaches idempotence/runbooks, checkpoint state, replay and backfills.
A recurring job will run again. If the second run appends the same business rows or depends on leftovers from the first,
automation creates corruption instead of saving time.
Coordinate discovery -> load -> transform -> validate -> publish as one rerunnable batch, keep raw inputs immutable, use
controlled output replacement/versioning, and record a run manifest.
L01-L08 mastered; C1 reproducibility basics familiar.
Imagine a photocopier with a RUN button. Pressing RUN twice should produce another copy of the intended report, not secretly
staple a duplicate set of pages into the business ledger.
5. New words before we use them
rerun - execute the same workflow again
idempotence - a property where repeating an operation does not create additional unintended effect
run manifest - record of versions, inputs, counts, checks and outputs for one run
immutable input - source data kept unchanged by processing
Book-led. pathlib/logging docs support implementation. The old venv video is removed from B02 active study because C3-00
Run a controlled good-path batch using a master copy you explicitly make unique only for demonstration (recording that the
source master remains invalid). Produce CSV/JSON evidence. Run it twice without changing inputs.
if any(c["critical"] and c["status"] == "FAIL" for c in checks):
raise RuntimeError("Critical validation failed; publish blocked")
Business-row count and output hash/content are stable across unchanged runs; source files remain unchanged; a new run
manifest records each run without duplicating business rows.

The pipeline separates append-only run evidence from replace/versioned business output. Repetition is planned rather than
- Append mode for a full-snapshot output.
- Second run succeeds only because first run created hidden temp state.
- Calling a workflow idempotent without defining the side effect being protected.
Define the side effect first: final business output. Make it a fresh snapshot file. Prove row count before adding any scheduling idea.
Change only output directory and rerun from clean process. The data result must match while run path/manifest reflects the
Two unchanged runs -> same business rows/totals; raw file hashes unchanged; manifest lists exact selected inputs and runtime
Explain idempotence in your own example and name one operation that is not automatically idempotent.
After review, inject a failed validation between transform and publish. Prove the previous good output is not overwritten by the failed run.
Save two run manifests, output row/total/hash comparison, source hashes, failed-run output-protection proof. PASS -> L10.
C2B DA-to-DE Bridge | B02 Python Pipeline Transition | INTERNAL QA RC1
B02-L10 - Build and defend a small reproducible batch
What you already know as an analyst: integrated notebook produces an analysis/report.
What changes in engineering: the artifact is a rerunnable system with contracts, controls, evidence and safe failure.
Why engineers care: C3 assumes you can reason about data moving through stages before it adds real ingestion, dbt, orchestration and
Small worked example: three sales files -> validated rows -> safe master join -> regional output + run evidence.
Real engineering version: C3-01 begins source->landing->staging, APIs, databases, incremental state, CDC and backfills.
Bridge mastery must prove you can combine the ideas, not just answer isolated questions. This lesson is the rehearsal for the
Build a small end-to-end local batch pipeline with explicit contract, deterministic discovery, parsing, merge safety, failure
containment, logging, validation, safe publish, rerun evidence and handoff.
Think of a transparent pipe with inspection windows. Data enters through named inputs; every stage has a check; a red gate
stops unsafe data; the final output comes with a receipt showing exactly how it was produced.
5. New words before we use them
pipeline - connected stages that move/transform data under explicit rules
handoff - evidence/instructions enabling another person to run and diagnose the work
critical failure - defect that makes publishing unsafe
defense - concise explanation of architecture, controls, failure behavior and limitations
No video required. Use the lesson as teacher; revisit only the exact prior source for the skill you cannot reproduce.
Build the pipeline using the provided practice data. The supplied duplicate C013 is a required failure: first prove the run blocks.
Then use a clearly documented, separate demonstration master (not silent repair of source) to complete the good-path rehearsal.
DISCOVER -> VALIDATE FILE SET -> LOAD -> PARSE/TYPES
First run stops safely on duplicate master. Good-path rehearsal produces validated output and evidence. Repeating unchanged
good inputs does not duplicate business rows.
C2B DA-to-DE Bridge | B02 Python Pipeline Transition | INTERNAL QA RC1
Every critical assumption is either declared or checked. Failure evidence is retained, and publish is downstream of validation.
- Editing customers.csv until the test passes.
- Publishing before validation because "the rest of the code needs an output".
- A manifest with filenames but no counts/check status/versions.
- Calling the capstone complete without a failure/recovery demonstration.
Build vertical slices: discovery+count first; then parse+reconcile; then master-key block; then good-path merge; then logs/checks; publish last.
Rebuild the same architecture on a fresh two-file mini-batch and a clean, separately created master. Keep function
names/contracts but do not copy final outputs.
Prove selected files, 96-row source control on full practice batch, I370,375 source net total, duplicate-key block, good-path row
preservation, validations, safe second run, manifest and no raw edits.
Give a 2-minute defense: input/output grain, stage boundaries, most dangerous failure, control that catches it, publish rule, rerun
Protected Review L10 only after attempt. Changed retry uses a fresh mini-batch; then complete B02 Mini-Lab from a clean copy.
Save project files, run evidence, validation JSON, two-run proof, failure/recovery proof and defense notes. PASS -> B02 Mini-Lab, then Gate A.

Which files/records were selected, and by what rule?
What does one row/object represent before and after each major stage?
Which columns/types are required, and what happens if they are wrong?
Is the master key unique? What cardinality is declared? Any unmatched keys?
Which failures BLOCK and which can be WARN/quarantine?
What did the run do? What checks proved trust?
What happens if the same inputs run twice?
Can another learner reproduce the run without hidden notebook state?

- If row count or control total changes after a merge, explain the cardinality before trusting any
aggregate.
- If a live HTTP call is unavailable, prove the parsing/shape/validation logic on the supplied offline JSON
rather than inventing a successful request.
- If a rerun changes a trusted output without a declared policy, the pipeline is not yet reproducible.

With the learner book closed, you can describe the full path - discover -> load -> validate ->
transform/merge -> validate -> publish -> log/manifest - and name the exact checks that prevent a bad
run from becoming a trusted output.

watchGuide.text:
C2B / B02
B02 Python Pipeline Transition
Astra active route - strong RC1 teaching preserved - assessment layer deepened
C2B / B02 / ASTRA PARITY RC4 / CHECKPOINT42
Page 1
Open in this order
1) Existing 10-lesson learner book -> 2) existing notebook practice -> 3) Quick Revision -> 4)
closed-book Practical Mastery Check -> 5) protected check review only after a genuine saved
attempt -> 6) changed retry -> 7) Gate A.
Why the learner book is preserved
The current B02 book already uses the required beginner-first engineering loop: why/picture/new
words/source/guided work/expected result/why/recovery/independent
retry/validation/teach-back/protected review/evidence. Rewriting it only to change a version label would
risk losing useful examples and source mappings.
What RC4 deepens
The weak layer was assessment depth. RC4 adds a separate Quick Revision, an action-based
non-gating mastery check, a protected changed-retry review, and deeper Gate A/B/C reviews computed
from the actual hidden fixtures.
Gate rule
A clean Gate A pass ends B02. Gate B/C are fresh remediation-only reassessments. They stay sealed
until the saved failed/developing Gate attempt, matching protected review, targeted repair evidence,
changed micro-proof and explicit reassignment required by the existing Mentor state machine.
Runtime boundary
Static QA can verify notebook JSON, Python code-cell syntax, fixture controls, source mappings, PDF
layout and package integrity. It does not claim that every learner machine has executed
Python/pandas/Requests, filesystem permissions, Excel engines or live HTTP successfully.

lineage.
- Schema/numeric contract: validate required columns/types; identify the malformed value explicitly;
preserve evidence rather than hiding it.

approved business rule.
- Merge contract: declare many-to-one and reconcile pre/post row count plus control totals. Explain any
row multiplication before aggregating.

a critical failure.
- Run evidence: log selected files, counts, checks, runtime/library versions, output status and
failure/recovery path.
- Rerun evidence: a second run must not double append or silently create a second competing trusted
output.
- Defense: explain input grain, output grain, why the checks are placed before publish, and what Course
3 adds later.

- Silent coercion/drop/dedupe that hides the injected defect.
- Merge before proving master-key uniqueness.
- Publishing a trusted output after a critical validation FAIL.
